headline: Deutsche Telekom, the German telecoms group, aims to use AI to save 2.5 billion euros in costs and earn 800 million euros from AI-related business by 2030, Intelligent CIO reports.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: Intelligent CIO reported the plan on 9 Oct 2026, before the window, and the Wall Street Journal original could not be opened; the figures are company targets.
importance_line: What changed is that a large European telecom is putting numbers on how much of its work AI will take over, which matters first to its customers and employees, then to its shareholders and rival telecoms, and the doubt is that the savings and revenue figures are targets and the reported results come without independent checking.
summary: Intelligent CIO reports that Deutsche Telekom is targeting 2.5 billion euros of indirect cost savings, measured against 2023, and AI-related business revenue outside the US of 800 million euros by 2030, up from an expected 250 million euros in 2026, by building automation into its network, customer service and software work. It adds that a Telekom AI agent reportedly cut its response to mobile-network congestion from several hours to about a minute, and that in its US business AI agents now deal with 40% of customer contacts, while the number of service calls has dropped by 55%.
notes: The Wall Street Journal original (HTTP 401) could not be opened; Intelligent CIO's 9 Oct 2026 report covers the same plan and is credited instead. It does not say where or when the targets were presented. Not carried in earlier editions.
